title: The verse called a mother
hookLine: a boy who couldn't name his father is taken in by a teacher: the thread ceremony as a second birth, with the Gayatri as mother
carry: the gayatri gives a second birth
tomorrow: why do we say Om bhur bhuvah svah first?
last: HE SENDS US OUT, AND CALLS US HOME.

lines: A BOY WHO CAN'T NAME HIS FATHER.
HE TELLS THE TEACHER THE TRUTH.
cards: A boy named Satyakama wants to study the Vedas, and the teacher will ask about his family line. So he asks his mother, Jabala.
She tells him the truth: she doesn't know who his father was; she was young and worked as a servant in many houses. Call yourself Satyakama Jabala, she says, my son.
He walks to the teacher Gautama and repeats it word for word. The teacher says: no one but a true brahmin could speak like that. Bring firewood.
I'll initiate you. Today: the verse at the heart of that initiation, and why an old law book calls it a mother.

teach.b: That initiation is the upanayana, the sacred thread ceremony, and at its heart the teacher passes on one verse: the Gayatri, in many families whispered into the student's ear under a cloth.
Older law books, like the Manusmriti, call that verse the Savitri, after Savitr, the god it speaks to. And the Manusmriti says something bigger.

The ceremony is a second birth, and in that birth, it says, the Savitri is the mother and the teacher is the father. That's why one who has received it is called dvija, twice-born. Now hear Satyakama again.

teach.h: A FATHER, AND A MOTHER TOO.
teach.b: One way to read the two together: the boy who couldn't name a father is given one, his teacher, and a mother too, the verse. So why does almost everyone call it the Gayatri?

teach.h: GAYATRI: THE NAME OF A METER.
teach.b: Gayatri is the name of its meter. Vedic tradition counts three lines of eight syllables: tat savitur varenyam, bhargo devasya dhimahi, dhiyo yo nah prachodayat.
Like a poem called a sonnet, it's named for its vessel; the hymn that opens the Rig Veda, to Agni, has the same shape.
Traditions have differed on who receives it: the law books speak of boys, and today many families and movements teach it to daughters and to anyone who asks.

teach.h: RECEIVING A VERSE IS A BIRTH.
teach.b: Underneath sits the teaching: in Hindu life, receiving a sacred verse is a birth. You're born once to your parents, and again into a way of seeing.

how: At the upanayana, the sacred thread ceremony, a teacher or parent passes the Gayatri to the student, in many families whispered into the ear; students also learn it as an example of the gayatri meter, and older texts call it the Savitri.

games.q: what does “the gayatri in context” mean?
o: a verse said only at a wedding
a verse a teacher gives at a second birth, called its mother
a verse named for the sage who first sang it

games.q: the two names — tap the pairs.

s: the word gayatri appears in the verse
the verse names Savitr and asks for thoughts to be stirred; it never names itself.
gayatri is the name of a meter
the verse is called by the name of its shape: three short lines.
the Manusmriti calls the Savitri a mother
in the second birth of the thread ceremony, it says, the Savitri is the mother and the teacher the father.

games.q: you're the teacher Gautama. a boy tells you he doesn't know who his father was. what do you do?
o: send him away until he can name his family
take him in: he told the truth
games.why: 'bring firewood, i'll initiate you,' Gautama says; the boy hasn't strayed from the truth. in that second birth, says the Manusmriti, the teacher is the father and the verse the mother.

practice: On each out-breath, count eight slowly in your head, one line of the meter; do it three times for three lines, then rest for a few natural breaths and begin again. If you lose count, start the line over.
As you count, think of whoever first gave you a prayer, a verse or a way of seeing: a grandparent, a teacher, a parent. If you pray, give thanks for them; if you don't, simply hold them in mind.

wordCard.voice: The Gayatri in context: named for its meter, called the Savitri in the law books, and the mother of a second birth. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the name of a Vedic meter of three short lines, which became the name of the verse in it.

carryVoice: Your line: the Gayatri gives a second birth. Named for its shape, and called a mother. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Chandogya Upanishad 4.4 (Satyakama Jabala asks his mother his lineage, tells the teacher Haridrumata Gautama the truth, and is accepted: 'fetch fuel, I will initiate you')
Rig Veda 1.1 (the hymn to Agni, in gayatri meter)
Manusmriti 2.170 (the second birth of the upanayana: the Savitri is the mother and the teacher the father)
